newsitem.title: USA: Federal securities suit reinstated vs Philip Morris.
newsitem.headline: Federal securities suit reinstated vs Philip Morris.

text.p: A New York judge on Wednesday reinstated a federal securities class action lawsuit against Philip Morris Cos. Inc. based on new evidence of alleged misrepresentations and omissions by the tobacco company, according to court filings.

In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs alleged that Philip Morris artifically inflated the price of the stock by suggesting to the public "through their statements that nicotine is not addictive (and) that smoking is entirely a matter of 'choice.'"
U.S. District Judge Michael Mukasey had dismissed the original complaint in September 1995, saying that "Philip Morris's statements were permissible statements of opinion."
In granting the motion to reinstate the lawsuit on Wednesday, the judge said it was likely the plaintiffs could not have presented new evidence before he issued his earlier opinion.

In his latest opinion, the judge cited newly discovered evidence that specifically identifies Philip Morris and tobacco industry documents discussing studies concerning whether cigarettes and nicotine are addictive.

"This new documentary evidence is of enough potential importance and volume that I probably would not have granted defendants' motion to dismiss had it been described in the initial complaint," Mukasey said.
"Most of this evidence is admissible ...as newly discovered evidence," Mukasey said in his 24-page decision.

The judge said the evidence submitted also identifies the tobacco company "discussing the manipulation of nicotine levels in cigarettes, sworn statements from three former Philip Morris researchers...discussing the companies alleged knowledge" of nicotine addictiveness and recent government actions declaring nicotine as as addictive drug.
